title: The loop reads the app's own menus
goal: Audits keep saying they could not check a menu name from the running app, so a person has to open the menu and check by hand. After this a scripted walk writes out the app's whole menu bar, and an audit quotes a menu item it really read.
notes: Done WITHOUT the Accessibility grant the task originally asked for. Reading another app's menus needs Apple Events or accessibility; the probe is our own app, so a new playtest step ("menus") walks NSApp.mainMenu and writes menus-<stage>.json and .txt into the walk's out folder. Step model: Sources/PhotonzCore/PlaytestScript.swift; driver: Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift (readMenuBar/describe(item:)/shortcut/outline). Ready-made walk: Scripts/playtest/menu-bar.json. Doc: docs/design/playtest-harness.md. NSMenu.update() runs on every submenu first, or titles that rename themselves report stale. Known limit: a walk never brings the probe to the front, so SwiftUI's window-scoped commands all report disabled; the reading says so in its first line and stops marking items dimmed rather than lying. The Accessibility grant is still unticked and still worth having the day something needs to drive an app that is not ours; Scripts/probe-app.sh still prints how.
acceptance: A scripted walk writes the running app's menu bar out as readable text, with every title, order and shortcut.
It works with no privacy grant at all, so the loop never waits on a person to tick a box.
An audit names a real menu item it read, not one it guessed from the source.

log.note: review before building: the task assumes reading a menu needs a grant only a person can give, but the app whose menus we want IS the probe. An app can enumerate its own menu bar with no permission. Nothing in the loop has ever needed to drive a third-party app, and the playtest harness already synthesizes keys, clicks and drags into the probe in-process, so a System Events bridge would be speculative. Shortest version that delivers the same value: one playtest step that dumps the live menu bar. It also survives the grant never being ticked, and does not break when the loop runs from a different terminal, which the accessibility route would.
built the menus step, TDD: two tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PlaytestScriptTests.swift red first, then the model, then the AppKit driver. Scripts/test.sh green, 1485 tests.

review of the built thing, on the real probe: first run reported every item dimmed because no window is key. Tried making the window key and activating the app; macOS refuses a background app the activation, and stealing focus from whoever is working would be the wrong fix anyway. So the step reports focus honestly and only marks dimming when something has focus. Second pass: the reading was only reachable by unpicking log.json, so it now also writes menus-<stage>.txt you can cat.

acceptance rewritten. The original first item was "probe-app.sh prints Accessibility granted", which is a solution, not an outcome, and the outcome turned out not to need it. The grant is still unticked; Scripts/probe-app.sh now says what it actually costs (driving apps that are not ours) instead of claiming menu titles need it.
audit queue/audits/2026-09-02-loop-reads-menus.json, with the real menu bar reading and a Screen Recording capture of the walk. Follow-up filed: show-history-and-hide-history-agree-with-whether.
